Do not use it for S3, EFS, FSx, instance store,\\\\n  or EC2 problems unrelated to EBS.\\\\nmetadata:\\\\n  author: dewavic\\\\n  version: \\\\\"1.0.0\\\\\"\\\\n  summary: \\\\\"Troubleshoot Amazon EBS performance, volume modifications, snapshots, encryption, quotas and cost, and review an account\\'s EBS setup with read-only checks.\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: \\\\\"CHAT, INCIDENT_RCA\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: \\\\\"Amazon EBS, Amazon EC2, Amazon CloudWatch, AWS CloudTrail, AWS Service Quotas\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: \\\\\"Storage\\\\\"\\\\n---\\\\n# Amazon EBS Expertise\\\\n\\\\nUse this skill to troubleshoot Amazon EBS problems and to review an account\\'s Amazon EBS setup. It has two modes. Troubleshoot mode answers \\\\\"something is wrong, why?\\\\\" through one of five paths and returns a fixed verdict. Review mode answers \\\\\"is my EBS setup healthy before something goes wrong?\\\\\" and returns a rated report. Both modes are read-only and share the same volume-type rules, instance limits and service rules. Load only the reference files the request needs.\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use This Skill\\\\n\\\\n- Storage-related slowness, timeouts or high I/O latency on an Amazon EC2 instance.\\\\n- An alarm on AWS/EBS metrics or on instance `EBSIOBalance%` / `EBSByteBalance%`.\\\\n- A request to raise IOPS or throughput, or to modify a volume.\\\\n- A volume modification that looks stuck, failed, or did not improve performance.\\\\n- Snapshot, AMI, Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager, AWS Backup or Recycle Bin questions, including which snapshots need owner review before deletion.\\\\n- Encrypted-volume access errors and AWS KMS questions for Amazon EBS.\\\\n- Amazon EBS cost increases, idle or over-provisioned volumes.\\\\n- An operation that failed on an Amazon EBS quota, or \\\\\"how close am I to my limits?\\\\\"\\\\n- A request to review Amazon EBS posture before a launch, migration or peak event.\\\\n\\\\nDo not use this skill for Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx, instance store, or Amazon EC2 issues unrelated to Amazon EBS.\\\\n\\\\n## Prerequisites\\\\n\\\\n- Read-only permissions for the APIs listed in [references/data-collection.md](references/data-collection.md).\\\\n- AWS CloudTrail access is optional. The skill works without it.\\\\n- Mutating changes run only through directed actions (Agent Actions in the Operator Web App), which need their own role and operator approval on the approval card.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Workflow\\\\n\\\\nCopy this checklist and tick each step as you finish it:\\\\n\\\\n- [ ] Step 1: Classify the request\\\\n- [ ] Step 2: Load the shared references\\\\n- Report\\\\n\\\\nFollow the numbered procedure in the loaded path. Discover every value from the APIs. Then draft the report in the format below.\\\\n\\\\n### Troubleshoot verdict format\\\\n\\\\n1. **Answer:** the asked question, answered first.\\\\n2. **Evidence:** values with units and time window.\\\\n3. **Binding layer:** Volume, Instance, Burst credits, Quota, Not EBS, AWS-side impairment (only with a direct signal, see [references/finding-logic.md](references/finding-logic.md)), Indeterminate, or Not applicable.\\\\n4. **Recommendation:** exact parameters, or \\\\\"No change\\\\\".\\\\n5. **Separate findings:** other true facts that do not change the Answer.\\\\n6. **Gaps:** what could not be checked and why.\\\\n\\\\nIn an investigation, put the Answer and the Recommendation with its exact parameters in the root cause finding, not only under Gaps. Keep the findings on the resource the user asked about. Mention another volume only when it shares the same instance EBS baseline, and then as a Separate finding.\\\\n\\\\nWhen the Binding layer is Indeterminate, report it as one finding. Do not offer AWS-side impairment as a hypothesis. List each direct check you ran (volume status, `VolumeStalledIOCheck`, AWS Health, AWS FIS) with its result as supporting evidence, say that no check confirms or rules out an EBS-side slowdown, and give the escalation path.\\\\n\\\\nReview mode uses the rated report in [references/review-report-format.md](references/review-report-format.md). Every Review mode response MUST begin with its Summary table, which rates all six areas (capacity and quota headroom, observability, cost hygiene, resilience, encryption posture, deletion protection), even when an area has no findings or is `Indeterminate`. The Summary table is required, not optional. Do not open with prose or an offer to run the review; start with the table, then the per-area detail.\\\\n\\\\n## Step 4: Check the Draft Before Presenting It\\\\n\\\\nReview the draft from Step 3 against these checks. Fix anything that fails, then present it.\\\\n\\\\n- Every number under Evidence came from an API call made in this session, has its unit and time window, and matches the resource ID it is attributed to.\\\\n- The Binding layer agrees with the Evidence: the named layer is the one at its limit, and the other layers were checked and shown to have headroom. The Evidence gives the instance EBS baseline in MiB/s and IOPS next to the summed demand of all attached volumes.\\\\n- Any Recommendation stays within the instance\\'s EBS baseline and the volume type\\'s documented limits, and it is not more provisioning for an impairment.\\\\n- Every snapshot tier is backed by the checks it requires; if one of those checks failed, the item is not listed for owner review. No snapshot is recommended for deletion; the owner confirms first.\\\\n- A review answer starts with the Summary table and rates all six areas.\\\\n- Every API that failed or was not called is listed under Gaps.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Critical Rules\\\\n\\\\n- **Read-only.** Changes (ModifyVolume, quota requests) are proposed with exact parameters, cost and rollback, and run only through operator-approved directed actions (Agent Actions in the Operator Web App). Approval is given only on the approval card. A typed \\\\\"approve\\\\\" in chat is not approval.\\\\n- **Deletes are manual customer steps.** AWS DevOps Agent refuses delete-class operations (for example DeleteSnapshot, DeleteVolume, DeregisterImage), so never propose them as directed actions. After the owner confirms they no longer need the resource, give the commands for the customer to run with their own credentials.\\\\n- **Answer in one reply.** In chat, run the checks in this conversation and return the finished verdict or report as your reply. Do not hand the work to a background sub-agent and reply with a \\\\\"started\\\\\" or \\\\\"I will report back\\\\\" message, because that message becomes the answer the user sees first.\\\\n- **Discover, don\\'t assume:** read every configuration value from the APIs.\\\\n- **Rule EBS in or out before tuning it.**\\\\n- **Answer the asked question first;** other findings go under \\\\\"Separate findings\\\\\".\\\\n- **Review mode starts with the Summary table.** Every Review mode response begins with the Summary table of all six rated areas. The table is required, not optional.\\\\n- **Always check the instance layer** and size changes within the instance\\'s EBS **baseline**.\\\\n- **Never recommend more provisioning for an impairment.**\\\\n- **Use current service rules:** up to 4 Elastic Volumes modifications per volume per rolling 24 hours. There is no fixed waiting period between modifications; the next one is allowed once the previous one completes.\\\\n- **No interpretation without data:** report what couldn\\'t be checked and use fallbacks. `DescribeVolumesModifications` returns only the most recent modification per volume; modification history and counts come from the optional AWS CloudTrail `ModifyVolume` events, or are listed under Gaps.\\\\n- **Units:** MiB/s for throughput, stated every time.\\\\n- **Escalate** on scope signals or when the investigation can\\'t explain the symptom.\\\\n\\\\n## Gotchas\\\\n\\\\n- A modification in `optimizing` is not stuck. The new size, IOPS or throughput already applies while it optimizes.\\\\n- `DescribeInstanceTypes` reports EBS bandwidth in MB/s. Convert it to MiB/s before comparing it with volume throughput.\\\\n- On io1 and io2, `VolumeThroughputPercentage` is the percentage of provisioned IOPS delivered. It is not a throughput signal.\\\\n- `VolumeAvgIOPS`, `VolumeAvgThroughput`, `VolumeAvgReadLatency` and `VolumeAvgWriteLatency` need both `VolumeId` and `InstanceId` and exist only on Nitro instances. `VolumeAvgThroughput` is in KiB/s. `VolumeTotalReadTime` and `VolumeTotalWriteTime` are in seconds.\\\\n- Rising latency and queue length with falling IOPS is not proof of an AWS-side impairment. Without a direct signal (failed `VolumeStalledIOCheck`, impaired volume status, or an open AWS Health event) and without a running AWS FIS experiment, the Binding layer is Indeterminate.\\\\n- `DescribeVolumesModifications` returns only the latest modification per volume. It cannot count modifications in the last 24 hours.\\\\n- `ListRecoveryPointsByResource` without `ManagedByAWSBackupOnly` set to true also lists snapshots that AWS Backup did not create.\\\\n- A snapshot whose source volume is gone may be the only remaining copy of the data. List it for owner review; never call it safe to delete.\\\\n- Snapshots are incremental, so deleting one may free less storage than its size suggests.\\\\n\\\\n## Error Handling\\\\n\\\\nErrors, gated reads and missing metrics are handled with the fallback table in [references/data-collection.md](references/data-collection.md). {"id": "7f6821ea-18d0-42b0-857d-5c4c2332fdda", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_51ZTbUt6wBlWPs6kWV7B70", "content": "[{'text': '# Troubleshoot: Elastic Volumes modification\\n\\n## When this path applies\\n\\n- \"My modification is stuck\", \"the new IOPS has not taken effect\", \"how long will optimizing take?\"\\n- A `ModifyVolume` call failed with an error.\\n- Sizing a resize, an IOPS or throughput change, or a gp2 to gp3 migration.\\n- Extending the file system after a size increase.\\n- Shrinking a volume or cancelling a modification.\\n\\n## Procedure\\n\\n1. **Find the volume.** Use the volume ID the user gives, or discover it with `DescribeVolumes` (by instance attachment or by the volumes that have recent modifications). Never pick a volume by its Name tag alone; confirm the ID with the user if more than one matches.\\n2. **Read the latest modification record.** `DescribeVolumesModifications` for the volume: `ModificationState`, `Progress`, original and target values (size, type, IOPS, throughput), `StartTime`, `EndTime`, `StatusMessage`. This API returns only the most recent modification request for each volume. Use it for the current or latest modification state, not for history.\\n3. **Answer the asked question first, in plain words.**\\n   - `modifying` or `optimizing`: not stuck. In `optimizing` the new configuration already applies and performance is between the source and the target. It completes on its own.\\n   - `completed`: done. The new values apply.\\n   - `failed`: read `StatusMessage` and translate it (step 5).\\n   - Duration is best effort. The Amazon EBS User Guide says a 1 TiB volume typically takes up to about six hours to modify, and some performance changes take more than 24 hours, for example when the volume is not fully initialized.\\n4. **Count the modifications in the rolling 24 hours.** Up to 4 per volume in a rolling 24-hour period. There is no fixed waiting period between modifications; the next one is allowed once the previous one completes. `DescribeVolumesModifications` cannot give this count, because it returns only the latest modification. Count the `ModifyVolume` events for the volume in the last 24 hours with the optional AWS CloudTrail `LookupEvents` call (filter on the volume ID as the resource name, or on the event name `ModifyVolume`). Report how many remain in the current window. As a cross-check, the latest record from step 2 should appear among those events if its `StartTime` is in the last 24 hours. If the lookup is denied or unavailable, record a Gap (\"the number of modifications in the last 24 hours could not be confirmed\") and do not state how many remain.\\n5. **Translate errors.**\\n   - io2 \"Iops to volume size ratio of ... is too high; maximum is 1000\": io2 allows up to 1,000 IOPS per GiB. To reach the target IOPS, the size must be at least target IOPS / 1,000 GiB. Propose that size together with the IOPS.\\n   - gp3: up to 500 IOPS per GiB, and throughput up to 0.25 MiB/s per provisioned IOPS. If a request breaks either rule, give the size or IOPS that satisfies it.\\n   - Size decrease: not allowed. Size can only increase. To get a smaller volume, create a new volume and copy the data.\\n   - Cancel: a submitted modification cannot be cancelled. Wait for it to complete; a reverse change then counts toward the 4 in 24 hours.\\n   - Limit reached: the 4 modifications in the window are used. The next one is possible when the oldest falls out of the rolling 24-hour window.\\n   - Older instance types or MBR volumes: check the Elastic Volumes requirements page.\\n6. **Size a new target.**\\n   - Keep it within the instance\\'s remaining EBS baseline: `DescribeInstanceTypes` baseline (converted to MiB/s) minus the measured usage of the other attached volumes.\\n   - gp2 to gp3: keep at least the gp2 volume\\'s current baseline IOPS (3 x GiB, minimum 100) and its measured throughput. gp3 includes 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s at any size; provision more only if measured demand needs it.\\n   - State how the target was computed.\\n7. **File system extension after a size increase.** Give the commands for the operator to run on the instance. Never execute them.\\n   - `lsblk` to see the device and partition\\n   - `sudo growpart /dev/<device> <partition-number>` if the volume has a partition\\n   - `sudo xfs_growfs -d <mount-point>` for XFS, or `sudo resize2fs /dev/<device-or-partition>` for ext4\\n   - Point to the extend-the-file-system guide for Windows and other cases.\\n8. **Separate findings.** If the instance caps what the volume can deliver, write that under Separate findings. Never phrase it as \"the modification failed\" when the record shows `optimizing` or `completed`.\\n\\n## Decision rules\\n\\n- The modification record decides the Answer. Performance metrics never override it.\\n- An instance ceiling is a Separate finding with its own recommendation (instance type change).\\n- Use the binding-layer tree in [finding-logic.md](finding-logic.md) only when the user also asks about performance.\\n\\n## What to report\\n\\nThe verdict template in [finding-logic.md](finding-logic.md). The Answer names the state and what it means. Evidence lists the record fields. Recommendation gives the exact next call, if any. Gaps list anything unreadable.\\n\\n## Safety rules\\n\\n- The agent never runs `ModifyVolume` on its own. It proposes it as a directed action, approved on the approval card. A typed \"approve\" in chat is not approval.\\n- The proposal includes: the exact call (`--volume-id`, and only the changed fields among `--size`, `--volume-type`, `--iops`, `--throughput`), the expected state sequence (`modifying`, `optimizing`, `completed`), how many of the 4 modifications in the rolling 24 hours remain after this change (only when step 4 confirmed the count; otherwise say it is unconfirmed), cost direction, and rollback.\\n- Rollback: after the change completes, a reverse change of IOPS, throughput or type is possible and counts toward the 4. Size cannot roll back.\\n- Recommend a snapshot before a type change or a large resize on a volume with data the user cannot lose.\\n\\n## Sources\\n\\n- Modify a volume: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-modify-volume.html\\n- January 2026 What\\'s New post: https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/01/amazon-ebs-up-to-four-volume-modifications/\\n- Monitoring modifications: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/monitoring-volume-modifications.html\\n- DescribeVolumesModifications (most recent modification request only): https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_DescribeVolumesModifications.html\\n- AWS CloudTrail LookupEvents: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/APIReference/API_LookupEvents.html\\n- Modification duration (1 TiB, about six hours, more than 24 hours): https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-modify-volume.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/monitoring-volume-modifications.html\\n- Requirements: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/modify-volume-requirements.html\\n- Extend the file system: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/recognize-expanded-volume-linux.html\\n- gp3 and gp2: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/general-purpose.html\\n- io2: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/provisioned-iops.html\\n- Amazon EBS-optimized instances: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-optimized.html\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_Qffr8e2EUYvP66e1OmWWjn", "content": "[{'text': '# Data collection: read-only APIs, metric math, errors and fallbacks\\n\\nLoad this file on every request. Every value in a verdict or a review comes from one of these calls. Tags are used for naming only, never as the source of a configuration value.\\n\\n## Read-only API allowlist\\n\\n| Service | APIs |\\n|---|---|\\n| Amazon EC2 | `DescribeVolumes`, `DescribeVolumeStatus`, `DescribeVolumesModifications`, `DescribeVolumeAttribute`, `DescribeInstances`, `DescribeInstanceTypes`, `DescribeInstanceAttribute`, `DescribeSnapshots`, `DescribeSnapshotAttribute`, `DescribeImages`, `DescribeFastSnapshotRestores`, `GetEbsEncryptionByDefault`, `GetEbsDefaultKmsKeyId`, `GetSnapshotBlockPublicAccessState`, `DescribeLockedSnapshots` |\\n| Amazon CloudWatch | `DescribeAlarms`, `DescribeAlarmHistory`, `GetMetricData`, `ListMetrics` |\\n| Service Quotas | `ListServiceQuotas`, `GetServiceQuota`, `GetAWSDefaultServiceQuota`, `ListRequestedServiceQuotaChangeHistoryByQuota` |\\n| Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager | `GetLifecyclePolicies`, `GetLifecyclePolicy` |\\n| Recycle Bin | `ListRules`, `GetRule` |\\n| AWS Backup | `ListBackupPlans`, `ListBackupSelections`, `GetBackupSelection`, `ListRecoveryPointsByResource` (always with `ManagedByAWSBackupOnly` set to true; without it the call also returns snapshots AWS Backup did not create), `ListProtectedResources` |\\n| AWS KMS | `DescribeKey`, `GetKeyPolicy`, `ListGrants` |\\n| AWS Cost Explorer | `GetCostAndUsage`, `GetDimensionValues` |\\n| AWS FIS | `ListExperiments`, `GetExperiment` |\\n| AWS Health | `DescribeEvents` |\\n| AWS Compute Optimizer (optional) | `GetEBSVolumeRecommendations` |\\n| AWS CloudTrail (optional) | `LookupEvents`. This call is optional. If it is denied or returns nothing, record a Gap and continue. Never make it a required step |\\n\\nNothing outside this list is called by the skill on its own. Mutating calls are proposals (see SKILL.md Critical rules).\\n\\n## Metric rules\\n\\nAWS/EBS publishes 1-minute data.\\n\\n| Namespace | Metrics | Dimensions |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| AWS/EBS | `VolumeAvgIOPS` (Ops/s), `VolumeAvgThroughput` (KiB/s), `VolumeAvgReadLatency` (milliseconds), `VolumeAvgWriteLatency` (milliseconds), `VolumeStalledIOCheck` (0 passed, 1 failed) | `VolumeId` AND `InstanceId`.
